content.transcript: Iron pills only absorb 10 to 15%. The rest just passes through you. I tracked my ferritin for 18 months. Ferrosisulfate, bisglycinate, floridax, thorn. My number went from 11 to 13 in a year and a half. Here's the part nobody told me. Your gut has a fixed number of DMT1 receptors. They're the doors that let iron into your bloodstream. Once they're full, that's it. You can take a 65 milligram pill. You can take a 150 milligram pill. Doesn't matter. The doors don't change. And there's a second trap. Higher doses spike a hormone called heptadone, which blocks absorption for 24 to 48 hours after you take them. So that big mega dose iron pill is actually absorbing less than a small one. The only fix is to skip the gut entirely. Caviar melt dissolves on your tongue in 30 seconds. The iron goes through your mouth tissue straight into the blood. Different pathway, different rules. Tap the link, read the science, decide for yourself.
